solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lawyer's polite refusal to pick up a state

parts.note: 'No, ta' is a polite British way of turning something down

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, so the word for a state is taken by ear rather than by spelling

parts.note: a republic is a state without a monarch

explanation.surface: A lawyer politely declines an offer to collect someone's state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is British for thanks. Said quickly after 'no ta', the state's name loses its first vowel to the ear, giving the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: This official witnesses signatures and certifies documents, a legal practitioner of a specific kind.

clue.text: How to say "one skilled in martial art from Japan" in Japanese

definitions.text: How to say "one skilled in martial art from Japan" in Japanese

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted from the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A phrasebook question: what is the Japanese for a martial arts expert?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and 'from' draws the five letters straight out of 'Japan in Japanese', across the word gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese term for a covert agent trained in martial arts is exactly the borrowed word English uses.

clue.text: Material benefit finally by being among the ascendant elite

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word benefit
being among puts the multiplication sign inside the other piece
in a down clue, ascendant means the word elite is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: by is the multiplication sign, an X, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Fabric gives a final benefit to anyone joining the rising elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascendant' turns ELITE into ETILE in this down clue; 'being among' puts X inside it, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven fabric is a material, the cloth sense of the word.

clue.text: Dropping a hint the original sin violated many such beliefs

indicators.note: dropping says the letters of 'a hint' are taken out of the pool before it is rearranged
violated means the remaining letters are abused into a new order

explanation.surface: Abandoning a hint, the original sin broke the rules of many faiths.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, H, I, N, T from THE ORIGINAL SIN; 'violated' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Faiths such as Christianity or Islam are systems of belief, hence beliefs in the plural.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 20
Attempt to follow experimental album is a pain

indicators.note: to follow places the word for an attempt after the scrambled letters
experimental suggests trying the letters of album in a new arrangement

parts.note: an attempt is a go, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: Trying to sit through an experimental album is a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experimental' reads like music criticism but signals the rearrangement; 'to follow' puts the attempt after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is an ache in the lower back, so it is literally a pain.

clue.text: Where one might study the end of tragic village in fiction

indicators.note: the end of picks the closing letter of the word tragic

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in The Archers, the long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A literary question about how a tragic tale set in a fictional village ends.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBRIDGE is the village of The Archers, a BBC radio soap about English country life.
explanation.definitionFit: The English university town is a famous place to study at a university.

clue.text: Home team in wellies, regularly away from home

parts.note: to be home is to be in

indicators.note: in puts the team inside the letters picked from wellies
regularly takes every other letter of wellies

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: The home side turn out in wellies, but regularly play away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' does double duty, echoed in the definition. 'regularly' takes alternate letters of wellies; 'in' puts the team inside them. XI, eleven, is a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished lives abroad, far from their own country.

clue.text: James content to chase cheese and beans

indicators.note: to chase is to come after, so the inner letters of James follow the cheese

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: content means the contents, the inner letters of James without its ends

explanation.surface: A shopping list: James is happy to go after cheese and beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy'; it means James's insides, AME.
explanation.definitionFit: These are young soybeans served in the pod, a Japanese bean dish.

clue.text: Shows off home in an elevated position with all-round views

parts.note: to crow is to boast, so shows off gives crows
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone shows off their home in a lofty spot with panoramic views.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast gives a view in every direction.

clue.text: Stay engrossed in paperback, being a slacker

indicators.note: engrossed in a book means inside it, so the word for stay goes inside

parts.note: read as paper back: a ream of paper, written backwards
to stay on is to linger

explanation.surface: A lazy reader lingers over a paperback instead of working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paperback' splits into paper (REAM) and back, turning it to MAER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who feigns illness to dodge work is a shirker, a slacker.

clue.text: Careful head demoted off course

indicators.note: the head letter of the word for careful is moved down a place

parts.note: careful means wary

explanation.surface: A cautious leader is demoted after going astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head demoted' moves the first letter, W, one place down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray or amiss has gone off course.

clue.text: Firm about left-wing principles

indicators.note: about means around, so the firm's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
red means left-wing, socialist

explanation.surface: A company has a set of left-leaning values.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or guiding tenets, principles.

clue.text: Noisy loving beneath chapel enclosure

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts the word for loving under the chapel letters
the enclosure of chapel is its outside letters, which enclose the rest

parts.note: amorous means loving

explanation.surface: Noisy lovemaking can be heard beneath the chapel walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' looks like a fenced yard; it is the outer letters of chapel, C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means loud and shouting, so noisy.

clue.text: Terms describing all recent Labour leaders as belligerent types

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the terms go around the leading letters

parts.note: terms are words

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters of all, recent and Labour

explanation.surface: Critics call every recent Labour leader warmongers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, drawing a line around something, and 'leaders' means first letters, not party chiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Military chiefs who rule by force are aggressive, warlike figures.

clue.text: Mother trapped by machinery part in elaborate procedure

indicators.note: trapped by puts the word for mother inside the other pieces

parts.note: a rig is apparatus or machinery, as in an oil rig
a part in a play is a role
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum got caught in some machinery during a complicated routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, fussy and pointless process is a palaver, an elaborate procedure.

clue.text: Standard names for melting cheese

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: melting suggests the word names losing its shape and reforming

explanation.surface: A standard label given to cheese for melting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting' belongs with cheese in the surface; it rearranges NAMES as MESAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard Italian cheese is grated over pasta; it is a type of cheese.

clue.text: Beast in military coup starts rounding up members of junta

indicators.note: rounding up puts those first letters around the other piece
starts picks the first letters of military and coup
the members of junta are its letters, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A brute takes part in a military coup, rounding up the junta.
explanation.walkthrough: M and C go round UNTJA, the letters of 'junta' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Asian deer is an animal, a beast.

clue.text: Clark's a bit off the wall

definitions.meaning: the surname of Clark, the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind
the triangular upper part of an end wall under a pitched roof

explanation.surface: Clark's behaviour is a bit eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the wall' looks like 'eccentric'; it is the literal part of a house wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was the film actor, and the gable end is the pointed section of a building's wall.

clue.text: Rural bum's endless gripe

indicators.note: endless means the word bum loses its last letter

parts.note: colic is a gripe, a sharp stomach pain

explanation.surface: A country tramp keeps complaining without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripe' looks like a complaint; it is the stomach-ache sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes the countryside and pastoral life, so rural.

clue.text: Feathers and foreign articles from the other side of the world

definitions.text: the other side of the world

parts.note: down is soft feathers
UN is French for 'a' and DER is German for 'the'

explanation.surface: Feathers and imported goods shipped from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods; it is grammar: UN (French) and DER (German).
explanation.definitionFit: This informal name for Australia and New Zealand reflects their position on the far side of the globe.

clue.text: See 25
Ex cathedra major play

indicators.note: ex means out of, so the word comes out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A grand play delivered with authority, ex cathedra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex cathedra' is Latin for speaking with authority, which hides the use of 'Ex'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece written for the stage is a play.

clue.text: Old union asked regularly to provide tender

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of asked

explanation.surface: A former union was regularly asked to make a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an offer; it means one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is someone who looks after others, as a carer does for patients.

clue.text: Libertine operating smartly dressed, initially up all night

indicators.note: dressed means wearing, so the word for operating is wrapped in the jacket

parts.note: dressing smartly means putting on a DJ, a dinner jacket
on means working, operating

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of up, all and night

explanation.surface: A rake goes about in evening dress, staying up all night.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ is British for dinner jacket, what Americans call a tuxedo.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Spanish seducer has become a byword for a womaniser, a libertine.

clue.text: Mean-sounding birds

parts.note: the bird-catchers' name is heard as a word for nastier people, those more foul

explanation.surface: A description of some nasty-sounding birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose cryptic definition: bird-catchers whose name sounds like 'foulers', meaner folk. Blog commenters were unsure of the parse too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters of wildfowl are named for the game birds they pursue.

clue.text: Feature of the pandemic might get Corbyn on the floor if first promoted

indicators.note: the first letter of the dancing word is moved up, earlier in the phrase

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn, former Labour leader, is a socialist
on the dance floor means dancing

explanation.surface: Imagine Jeremy Corbyn, the former Labour leader, dancing during lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if first promoted' lifts the D of DANCING three places, in front of IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping two metres apart was a rule of the Covid-19 era, a feature of the pandemic.

clue.text: Make secure?

indicators.note: make means form or fashion, so the letters of secure are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A short question: is the aim to make something safe?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' does two jobs: anagram signal and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is to make them safe, keeping them secure.
